subject.title: [Feature] Allow per-binding tool restrictions (tools.deny) in route/ACP bindings

question: Should OpenClaw add binding-scoped `tools.allow`/`tools.deny` as a supported core config/security boundary for route and ACP bindings, or should operators use existing group/sender/session policy surfaces instead?
rationale: This adds a new public security-control config surface and precedence model across route matching, ACP bindings, Gateway tool resolution, embedded-agent tool construction, and existing policy layers; automation cannot safely choose that contract.

options.title: Design binding-scoped policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and regression proof before implementation.

options.title: Use existing policy surfaces
options.body: Decline the new binding key and document group/channel, sender, session, and per-agent policy as the supported way to restrict tools.

options.title: Defer to identity/session work
options.body: Block this on the broader scoped session or conversation identity design if maintainers want one authorization model instead of a binding-specific slice.

recommendation.title: Design binding-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and regression proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent scoped conversation capability profile and adjacent tool-policy/security work make this the strongest available decision-owner signal.
